title: BugHerd vs Marker.io
kicker: · BUGHERD VS MARKER.IO · COMPARED FOR AGENCIES
headline: BugHerd vs Marker.io: which fits your agency?
standfirst: Both collect website feedback with a pin and a screenshot. The fork: BugHerd keeps feedback on the page and manages it on its own board. Marker.io turns feedback into tickets inside the tracker your team already runs.
disclosure: We make Superflow, a third option in this space. It appears once, at the end, clearly marked. Everything above it is a straight comparison.
dateline: Facts checked July 2026, from bugherd.com and marker.io.
shortAnswerPickLeft: if you want feedback pinned on the live page and managed on a built-in board, with clients commenting free.
shortAnswerPickRight: if the fixes live in Jira, GitHub, or Linear and your developers never want to leave, and you want console logs and session replay attached to every report.
shortAnswerShared: Both assume a person finds every mistake.

dimensions.label: Who checks the site
dimensions.framing: Start with the question everything else depends on.
leftFacts: A person finds every issue, then pins it.
rightFacts: A person finds every issue, then reports it.
Its AI translates, retitles, and rewrites report text; it does not look at the site.
dimensions.verdict: Even. In both tools, the checking is a person's job. That is the premise the third option removes.

dimensions.label: How the client says yes
dimensions.framing: Both make commenting easy. Neither makes the yes formal.
leftFacts: Guests comment free from a link, no account.
A formal approval flow: not yet verified.
rightFacts: Reporters submit free from the widget, no account.
Ongoing client collaborators are paid guest seats.
A formal approval flow: none found on marker.io, July 2026.
dimensions.verdict: Comment collection: even, both good. A recorded client sign-off: neither, pending verification.

dimensions.label: Where you review
dimensions.framing: On the page, or on a picture of the page.
leftFacts: Pins live on the site itself and stay through changes.
rightFacts: You annotate a captured screenshot of the page; the report carries the picture, not a persistent on-page pin.
Widget on the live site, extension for members.
Behind-login behavior on both: not yet verified.
dimensions.verdict: Persistent on-page review: BugHerd. Capture-and-file: Marker.io. Different philosophies more than a ranking.

dimensions.label: What stays private
dimensions.framing: Your team needs somewhere to disagree.
dimensions.verdict: As verified today: Marker.io. Firms up once BugHerd's dash resolves.

dimensions.label: What gets captured
dimensions.framing: Both capture context. One captures much more of it.
leftFacts: Browser, OS, and screen size attach to every pin.
rightFacts: Console logs, network requests, and session replay attach on the Team plan and up.
dimensions.verdict: Technical depth: Marker.io, and it is not close. If your developers debug from reports, this dimension may decide the page.

dimensions.label: What it remembers
dimensions.framing: Does project ten start smarter than project one?
leftFacts: No memory concept. Each project starts blank.
rightFacts: No memory concept. Each project starts blank.
dimensions.verdict: Even: neither. Worth knowing before you invest years of client history in either.

dimensions.label: How it fits your stack
dimensions.framing: The biggest difference is where the feedback goes.
leftFacts: Feedback pins to the page and stays there. The kanban is built in. The tool is the workspace.
Integrations: Jira, Trello, Asana, ClickUp, Slack, Teams.
rightFacts: Feedback becomes a ticket in your tracker. The dashboard is a waypoint; the tracker is the workspace.
Thirteen-plus integrations, dev-side especially: GitHub, GitLab, Linear, Bitbucket; Jira from the Team plan; Azure DevOps on Business.
dimensions.verdict: Self-contained studio: BugHerd. Tracker-centered dev shop: Marker.io. Note the plan gates: Jira costs Marker.io's Team tier.

dimensions.label: What it costs
dimensions.framing: The sticker and the math are different numbers.
leftFacts: $50 / $80 / $150 per month, 5 / 10 / 25 members, +$8 per extra member.
Guests free, no page-view caps advertised.
rightFacts: Starter $39/mo annual (3 users, 10 projects, 5k page views/mo). Team $149 annual (15 users, 50 projects, 25k page views/mo).
Agency plan $129/mo, $99 annual: 15 members, 50 projects, 50 guests, conditions apply.
dimensions.verdict: Lowest entry: Marker.io, if the caps fit. Predictable at client scale: BugHerd. Agencies should price Marker.io Agency against BugHerd Studio, caps included.

thirdOptionBody: Both BugHerd and Marker.io assume a person finds every mistake. Superflow is a QA tool + a team: AI agents built from your checklist check every site change, pin what they find, your team decides, and your client approves from a link. No account, no login, no app, from their phone.

faq.question: Which is better for a small agency?
faq.answer: BugHerd if feedback should live on the page with clients commenting free; Marker.io if your fixes live in a tracker and you want technical context attached.

faq.question: Do clients need accounts?
faq.answer: No on both. BugHerd guests comment from a link; Marker.io reporters submit without an account. Ongoing client collaborators are paid seats on Marker.io.

faq.question: Which is cheaper?
faq.answer: Marker.io starts lower ($39 annual); BugHerd is simpler to predict at client scale (guests free, no page-view caps advertised). Price the caps.

faq.question: Can either check the site itself?
faq.answer: No. Both collect what a person found. Marker.io's AI edits report text; nothing in either tool looks at the site. That's the third option above.

faq.question: Which handles developer handoff better?
faq.answer: Marker.io: console logs, network requests, session replay, and the dev-tracker integrations are its center of gravity.
